answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are funnel-quality problems, not price problems. Onboarding is upstream of activation, so simplifying/shortening onboarding is the single lever most likely to move both, and it is the direction with the most mutually corroborating inherited evidence (memory_31 on signup field reduction and memory_86 on shortened onboarding, from different sessions and different points in time). I verify memory_86 because it is the most load-bearing for the chosen action and its recorded 'lift in early adoption' may be a short-window completion metric rather than durable value, and memory_91 because activation messaging is the nearest competing option and I want to know whether its week-one engagement gain persisted past week one before discarding it. I deliberately do not choose promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records exactly that shape of result -- large headline conversion and revenue lift concentrated in a low-touch segment, with -12pp later-cycle retention -- and it was explicitly consolidated as not repeatable. Matching a price attack with discounts would buy accounts that churn, which is the opposite of the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. Referral incentives (memory_57) are sound but address neither current decline and depend on an established base rather than the leaking SMB funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a real finding but aimed at a segment that is not the one under pressure this week. Key residual uncertainties I am carrying rather than resolving: the inherited onboarding results predate the competitor's entry, so the current declines may be competitive attrition of price-sensitive accounts rather than friction, in which case an onboarding fix will underperform its historical effect; and the same low-touch-segment quality risk that spoiled the promo test could apply here, since removing signup friction can admit weaker accounts. I therefore run it as a standard experiment with retention and qualified-revenue readouts held open past the first cycle, not just completion and activation rates, and I will not treat an early completion lift as a win on its own. If verification shows memory_86's lift was measured only on a short window or memory_91 shows durable rather than week-one-only gains, I will reconsider in favor of activation_messaging.
